memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Maya naturally asked for Delta to be included and selected it as the leading option when its nonstop schedule and fare were reasonably comparable, while retaining a less expensive American itinerary as the backup.

messages.content: I need to sort out Philadelphia next. The workshop is Tuesday, July 21 through Thursday, July 23 in Center City. It starts at 8:30 Tuesday and ends at 4:30 Thursday. I can leave MSP after 3:30 Monday, and airfare needs to stay under $700.
I’ll compare Monday evening departures with Thursday returns that leave enough time to get from Center City to PHL. Are you checking a bag, and should I limit this to nonstop flights?
Carry-on only. Nonstop is strongly preferred, but show me a connection if it creates a meaningfully better schedule or price.

Understood. On Monday, the useful nonstop choices are a 4:45 p.m. departure arriving at 8:19 p.m. and a 5:20 p.m. departure arriving at 8:57 p.m. A 6:10 p.m. connecting itinerary does not arrive until 11:46 p.m., so it offers no practical advantage before the 8:30 start.
Agreed, skip the connection. What does Thursday look like after 4:30? I don’t want a return that only works if everything goes perfectly.

The 6:35 p.m. nonstop is too exposed. Even with a car waiting, workshop wrap-up and traffic could leave less than an hour at the airport. The realistic returns are 7:35 p.m., arriving MSP at 9:44 p.m., or 8:05 p.m., arriving at 10:12 p.m. Recent Thursday traffic estimates put Center City to PHL at roughly 25–45 minutes.
Build the combinations around those two returns. Include Delta if it’s competitive; I’d lean that way when the schedule and fare are close.

Two combinations fit. Option one is Delta nonstop both ways: MSP 5:20 p.m. Monday to PHL 8:57 p.m., then PHL 8:05 p.m. Thursday to MSP 10:12 p.m., for $548 round trip in standard economy. Option two is American nonstop both ways: MSP 4:45 p.m. to PHL 8:19 p.m., then PHL 7:35 p.m. to MSP 9:44 p.m., for $512.
How much usable airport time does each return give me? Assume I keep my bag with me at the workshop and can leave within ten minutes.

Leaving at 4:40 p.m., a typical arrival at PHL would be about 5:10–5:25, with 5:40 plausible in heavier traffic. That gives the 7:35 flight about 1 hour 55 minutes to 2 hours 25 minutes at the airport. The 8:05 flight gives about 2 hours 25 minutes to 2 hours 55 minutes. Both are workable with carry-on only, but the later flight has the stronger buffer.
Is there any catch with the Delta fare versus the American one? Basic economy would explain the difference.

Neither quoted fare is basic economy. Both include advance seat selection and a standard carry-on. The Delta fare is $36 more and returns 30 minutes later; its main practical benefit here is the extra transfer margin. The American combination gets you home 28 minutes earlier and costs less, but leaves less room for a delayed workshop exit or slow traffic.
Then make Delta the leading option and American the backup. Don’t book anything yet. Give me the exact two itineraries and the Thursday departure plan to carry forward.

Carry forward these two unbooked options for July 20–23. Leading option: Delta standard economy, nonstop, departing MSP Monday at 5:20 p.m. and arriving PHL at 8:57 p.m.; returning Thursday at 8:05 p.m. and arriving MSP at 10:12 p.m.; $548 round trip. Backup: American standard economy, nonstop, departing MSP Monday at 4:45 p.m. and arriving PHL at 8:19 p.m.; returning Thursday at 7:35 p.m. and arriving MSP at 9:44 p.m.; $512 round trip. On Thursday, keep the carry-on at the workshop, leave by 4:40 p.m., and have a car staged nearby. Expect PHL around 5:10–5:25, or approximately 5:40 in heavier traffic. Both fares remain below the $700 allowance, and neither has been booked.
